history.summary: Migration notes + the upgrade path, verified against a real v0.2.4 project. The fixture under tests/fixtures/v024-project/ is not a reconstruction: fourteen components as `git archive v0.2.4` produces them, a loom.config.json, a .loom/ cache and a page written in the vocabulary those manifests declared. Running the seven documented steps against it took it from 111 audit findings to ONE warning — and that warning is the landmark rule firing on a date-picker popup inside <main>, which the registry's own reference markup would trip the same way (1.0R-17). THREE CLI DEFECTS HAD TO BE FIXED FOR THE PATH TO EXIST AT ALL. (1) A v0.2.4 project's first contact with the 1.0 CLI was `No faqir.config.json found. Run 'faqir init' first.` — advice that writes a second config with an empty installed list beside a ui/ full of components; missingConfigMessage() reads the legacy config and names the rename instead, at all 17 call sites from one function. (2) `faqir init --force` reset installed to empty, so "refresh the engine" was impossible without hand-editing the config; it now keeps the inventory, remote registries and bundle settings and rewrites only what the registry owns. (3) THE BACKFILL WAS DESTROYING THE UPGRADE IT EXISTED TO ENABLE: it snapshotted TODAY's registry at TODAY's version, so the next `upgrade` compared the registry against itself and reported all 53 components up to date. It now snapshots the project's own copy at the version that copy's manifest records — the only honest baseline available, flagged backfilled, with a warning that says edits made before the store existed are part of it. FOURTH, AND THE ONE THAT SURPRISED: `upgrade` stopped trusting version numbers. 24 of the 53 components a v0.2.4 project holds ship CHANGED BYTES UNDER AN UNCHANGED VERSION (dialog, toast, accordion, drawer, tooltip had controller + stylesheet + markup rewritten while staying at 1.0.0), and the version-equality fast path skipped every one of them permanently; the merge decides now, and a same-version upgrade says so in the report. THE "NO UNDOCUMENTED BREAKING CHANGE" GATE IS THE REAL WORK: a changelog cannot be checked against itself, so tests/fixtures/v024/surface.json pins what the release HONOURED — every attribute value each component's manifest declared or its stylesheet/controller selected on — extracted from the tag by scripts/gen-v024-surface.mjs through extractSurface, the SAME function the test runs against today's registry (a diff run by two readers proves only that the two readers agree). Five components lost vocabulary; three had never said so, and this task wrote the entries: date-picker shipped the calendar extraction as a MINOR bump with NO changelog at all, losing seven parts (now 2.0.0, breaking); patterns/empty-state replaced data-part=action/secondary-action with `actions` across 0.9-04 and 1.0R-07 while STAYING AT 1.0.0, and had been trimmed to data-size=sm while its own sheet still styles md and lg — so faqir audit rejected markup the sheet renders (now 2.0.0, sizes declared again, the leftover lg rule pointed at the slot that exists); table's 1.x manifest declared data-variant=true|false, values no selector ever matched, recorded in its 2.0.0 note as the correction it was. docs/migration-1.0.md is authored prose (the EDIT a break needs is a human sentence) with a derived obligation: nine breaking entries, nine marked sections, checked both ways. Published at migration/ with the rename table and the seven steps rendered from src/migration.ts — the constants the end-to-end test EXECUTES, in the order it records — and the per-break sections rendered from the document's own prose; the markdown is served verbatim beside it like the spec's. NOT in the top nav (1.0R-09: nine links at 1280 with overflow hidden). 3,668 bun tests (+32), typecheck, all seven check gates, audit:registry, size, smoke, axe on the new page in both schemes, layout ratchet re-recorded at 195 pages with the new page at 0/0 and every other total unchanged. Five mutations seeded and observed to fail individually. Three follow-ups filed: 1.0R-16 (three components ship an rgba() shadow the audit calls an error, and audit:registry never runs the CSS rule set over its own stylesheets), 1.0R-17 (landmark treats an anchored popup as a modal), 1.0R-18 (add/upgrade disagree about which empty-state a project installed).

The `unknown-component` rule, and the seven data-ui values it found in Faqir's own registry. `<div data-ui="datatable">` audited CLEAN because every per-component rule is answered by a manifest and `html-audit.ts` skips a name it has none for — a skip that is HALF RIGHT (a registry component this project has not installed must not error) and hid the framework's single most likely failure mode. The distinction is not in the manifests a caller happens to hold: a new optional `HtmlAuditInput.knownUiValues` carries every data-ui value Faqir DEFINES, and a caller that cannot produce it does not get a guess (the 0.9-05 stance, asserted in both directions because "silent" and "never ran" look identical from outside). Known is FOUR sources: component directories, ALIASES (`alert` is `callout` — which is why the set is read from the manifests and NOT from registry-index.json, whose entries have no aliases field), base-layer values (`prose`, 1.0R-10), and — found on the rule's first run against the registry — the COMPANION values a component's own stylesheet defines: `button-group`, `input-group`, `radio-group`, `radio-label`, `checkbox-label`, `switch-label`, `heading`. Seven shipped data-ui values with no manifest anywhere, four used by patterns; `add button` + `faqir audit` reported button.html as broken until they were derived — from the STYLESHEETS, never from the markup under audit, so a typo in the audited file cannot legitimise itself (pinned on a synthetic registry, since in the real one every companion appears in both). Documenting them is follow-up 1.0R-13. Severity `warning` chosen not defaulted (a mixed-framework page stays exit-zero), no `fix` (the closest NAME is a guess and `faqir repair` applies fixes), and the escape hatch is a new generic `faqir audit --skip-rules <ids>` named in the message, in `--rules`, in SKILL.md and on the site. The plan's own example `datatable` gets NO suggestion and that is correct — nothing is within suggestClosest's three edits of it. Browser: `createAuditor(manifests, styles, knownUiValues)` — explicit, because deriving "the registry" from a page's payload is right only for a complete payload — a fifth rule scope `markup+registry`, and the generator ships `window.__FAQIR_UI_VALUES__` from the SAME `knownUiValues` the CLI calls, so the playground cannot disagree with `faqir audit`. The legend became `getHtmlRuleInventory()`, so the row arrived with no site edit. `audit:registry` and the reference sweep arm the rule — a gate promising "every rule a fragment can satisfy" cannot leave one unarmed. 3,564 bun tests, every check gate green; six mutations seeded and observed to fail individually.

Theme preview parity + the data-ui="prose" decision. TWELVE manifests declared `preview: "<name>.preview.html"`; SEVEN existed. The field is REQUIRED by the frozen schema and relaxing it would drag SPEC-1.0.md §8.2 plus src/protocol.ts's mirrored amendment table into a task whose Touches names neither — so the field stayed and the FILE became the obligation. `src/theme-preview.ts` renders the gallery once and `gen:theme-previews` writes the five missing (brutalist, default, document, midnight, paper); the other seven stay hand-authored on purpose (contrast paints every focus ring, document-serif is a signed agreement, glass needs a gradient to be translucent against) and BESPOKE_PREVIEWS names them so generated ∪ bespoke covers the theme set with no gap. BOTH writers now guarantee the file: gen-theme-manifests refuses a manifest whose preview is absent, and `faqir theme generate` — which declared a preview it never wrote, for every theme it will ever generate — writes one per theme AND per --document companion, INLINED not linked, because `themes/` there is a drop folder with no registry beside it (141 KB, self-contained). Found in passing: gen:theme-manifests was silently STRIPPING the $schema ref add-schema-refs.mjs adds; it writes it itself now and the twelve regenerate byte-identical. Second half: `data-ui="prose"` was invisible to agents — defined in registry/base/prose.css, used on a dozen pages of Faqir's own site, no manifest, so in NO manifest-derived surface. src/base-layer.ts DERIVES it (a data-ui some base stylesheet selects on that no component claims — today exactly prose; rhythm.css's dozen component selectors correctly yield none), documented as styling rather than given a manifest, on four surfaces: shipped SKILL.md, a project's .faqir/SKILL.md under THAT project's output dir (ui/base/prose.css), llms.txt + llms-full.txt, and components/index.html — the page a reader searched and found nothing on, and which is itself built out of prose. prose.css also violated Strict Rule 2 IN THE BASE LAYER: `max-width: 65ch` against a --measure-prose whose value is exactly 65ch. Two sweeps guard it, scoped to the file because the rest of the registry writes block-axis physical properties by convention; both exemptions are by construction — border WIDTHS have no token ladder here (matching 1px to --space-px would swap a spacing token into a border) and overflow-inline is an axis keyword, not a rename. 3,534 bun tests, every check gate, layout ratchet unchanged, 251 docs-site axe scans green. Nine mutations seeded and observed to fail individually.

The engine got a page and the two layout URLs stopped being one keystroke apart. `engine/index.html` is authored prose and live examples around five GENERATED tables — 17 directives, 18 modifiers, 11 magics plus the named internal, the PRIORITY ladder, the KEY_MAP aliases, the MOTION_PRESETS, the `$<name>` controller API off the `ctrl` literal and a row per plugin — read through the same parsers 1.0R-03 wrote for references/directives.md, so the site and the skill are two renderings of one vocabulary rather than two lists. The page loads scripts/faqir-core.js, so its examples ARE the engine running. NEW tests/generator/engine-page.test.ts mounts every authored example under faqir-core.dev.js (one engine per file, per the dev-build convention) and asserts it binds, reacts and draws ZERO diagnostic: the counter counts, `.trim` puts the trimmed value in the scope, the keyed list reconciles a removal by key and then reveals its `l-if` empty state, `l-show` flips and stamps `data-motion`, and `l-source` loads the site's own api/messages payload and renders a row per message. THAT TEST FOUND A SHIPPED BUG ON ITS FIRST RUN: `parseGuideExamples` ended an example at the FIRST `</template>` — fine for spacing/density, wrong for the first guide whose examples are templates, since `l-for` and `l-if` ARE `<template>` directives, so the keyed-list example shipped truncated at its own l-for's closing tag. It audited clean anyway (the audit tolerates an unclosed element) and rendered as something (a browser closes what the author did not). The extractor now counts depth and renderGuideExamples mounts from the same scan. A second latent bug fell out of the same page: replaceGuideMarker passed its block to String.replace as a STRING, which reads `$&` and `$<name>` as substitution patterns — and the l-source controller is literally called `$<name>`, so the engine table ate it; it is a replacer function now. THE ROUTE HALF WAS A JUDGEMENT CALL, ARGUED RATHER THAN DEFAULTED: the lab moved /layouts/ → /responsive/ and the guide keeps /layout/, and the retired URL is a SIGNPOST, NOT A REDIRECT — a 301 fixes the bookmark and keeps the defect, because anyone landing on /layouts/ may have been aiming at /layout/, and quietly serving them the lab is the confusion the task removes. The signpost names both destinations, carries noindex, and is filtered out of the sitemap. Asserted as a PROPERTY over the whole published route set rather than for the one pair: every pair of top-level routes is ≥ 2 keystrokes apart by Levenshtein (the ruler itself checked), with the retired path the single exemption — because it is the exemption. Also: no page, nav entry or sitemap row points at a retired path; site/content/layouts.html → responsive.html; home and docs/docs-site.md follow. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the engine is in every page's sidebar and on the home page but NOT in the top nav — that bar is `overflow: hidden` with nine links at 1280, a tenth would clip an existing one silently, and the layout ratchet cannot see a clip. Verified: 3,516 bun tests, typecheck, check:docs (331 files), check:skill, check:registry-index, check:audit-browser, check:schema-refs, size, audit:registry, check:bindings; a11y green on engine/responsive/layouts in both schemes (six timeouts in the full 20-minute run were load flakes and pass on re-run); layout budget re-recorded at 194 pages with the three new/moved pages at 0/0/0 at BOTH viewports and every ratcheted total unchanged. Five mutations checked: a dropped directive row, a dropped magic row, a trimmed plugin `provides`, a route one keystroke from another, a sitemap advertising a retired path, and a signpost linking one destination twice — the last two only after tightening the assertions, which is how the first pass of each was found to pass a broken page (the nav shell and the priority paragraph both name what the deleted TABLE ROW named).

The five scaffolds get a gallery generated from SCAFFOLDS, and admin-dashboard/internal-tool get real builders composed out of the patterns' own @ui:scaffold blocks (303 lines of hand-written, audit-failing markup deleted). Recorded here by 1.0R-09: the work shipped in 4785b4f with every acceptance box ticked, but the index cell and this cursor were never flipped.

Spent the budget 1.0R-06 recorded: 375×812 bleeds 52 → 29, with all five target pages at ZERO and 1280×900 re-recorded identically on all five counts (the 968-case desktop matrix for the touched components is byte-identical too, so nothing was traded). Every fix is intrinsic, per the doctrine the framework teaches — flex-wrap, max-inline-size, min-inline-size, overflow-wrap — and `breakpoint-canon` sees no new width prelude because none was added. `pagination`: the numbered nav neither wrapped nor had a ceiling, and an `inline-flex` root is sized by its content, so the row set the width. `key-value`: a 24-character IBAN IS the `1fr` track's min-content, so one unbreakable value sized the whole grid and every later row bled with it — `overflow-wrap: anywhere` rather than `break-word`, because only `anywhere` lowers the min-content contribution the track is floored by. `empty-state`: the centred cluster overflowed past BOTH edges, the inline-start half unreachable at any scroll position. BOTH JUDGEMENT CALLS CAME OUT 'same mechanism, fix them': `input-otp` (six `lg` segments and their gaps are 372px, wider than a 375px window before the page gutter; the transparent input is `inset: 0` so it follows whatever box the segments settle into) and `menubar`'s trigger bar (the same unwrapped row, 198px past its own example page). THE REAL CAUSE OF empty-state's BLEED WAS CONTRACT DRIFT, NOT A MISSING DECLARATION: 0.9-04 aligned the pattern's markup and slots onto the declared `actions` cluster but left the sheet styling `action`/`secondary-action` — parts nothing renders — so the slot that exists had no rule of its own and inherited a non-wrapping row from the PRIMITIVE of the same name (0.9-13's unresolved collision). Both sheets now style `actions` and the pattern's manifest template stops emitting the two phantom parts, so `faqir add` cannot reproduce the defect. NEW: tests/visual/narrow-fit.pw.ts — the wall beside the ratchet, per component, no budget, affordable only because the set is at zero. Each reference is mounted ALONE (buildPageHtml, shipped bytes) at 320 and 375, and again in a container 60% of its own max-content width. THE SECOND QUESTION IS NOT DECORATION: `menubar` fits a 375px window in isolation at 229px wide and still bled 198px on a page offering it 343, so a window-only check would have pinned nothing for it — and measuring max-content on `<main>` does not work either, because pagination/input-otp root at `inline-flex` and their demos share one inline formatting context, making main's max-content the whole row laid end to end. Each root is therefore sized to `max-content` on its own. All five fixes are pinned by a case that reverts exactly that declaration and asserts the named box reappears, then re-runs the page unbroken and expects silence; all five bite. DEFERRED, WITH A REPRODUCTION: `menubar`'s open submenu is a different mechanism — an anchored dropdown with no viewport clamp. Making the bar wrap took the example page to 0 by moving the anchor, not by clamping the panel; a five-trigger bar at 375 wraps so the open group lands mid-row and the submenu still paints 44px past the edge. Filed as 1.0R-12 as the family question it is (context-menu, dropdown-menu, select-custom, popover, tooltip anchor the same way, and the ratchet cannot see any of them because every one is closed on its example page). ALSO REPAIRED: the index cells for 1.0R-05 and 1.0R-06, which shipped with every acceptance box ticked but were never flipped to ✅. Verified: bun test 3482/0, typecheck clean, full playwright 4291/0, a11y 2985/0, audit:registry zero findings across six rule sets, all six generated-artifact checks up to date, layout gate + wall green on three consecutive runs. The one baseline that moved is the proof: responsive-pattern-empty-state-390 was 399px WIDE at a 390px viewport and is now 390. The layout ratchet gained a second ruler, and the second ruler found that the first one had been reporting a phone-width site nobody measured. `layout-budget.json` is now one section per viewport (`{viewports: {"1280x900": {...}, "375x812": {...}}}`, widest first); `summarize` returns one section, `compareBudget` still compares WITHIN a viewport, and the new `compareBudgets` runs the ratchet per section so a fall at 1280 cannot pay for a rise at 375 (pinned in both directions, plus the trade-off case). Two bookkeeping states the shape creates are decided rather than left implicit: a viewport measured but not yet budgeted is `unbudgeted` and PASSES (a rise against a section that does not exist would have deadlocked update mode against its own refusal to record one), while a viewport budgeted and no longer measured FAILS — a sweep that quietly drops a viewport reports a perfect site. Same Playwright job, same file, ~7s more: `beforeAll` sweeps `VIEWPORTS` in one context each. MEASURING 375 HONESTLY COST TWO COLLECTOR RULES AND A FLAKE FIX, all three forced by real evidence and none of them touching a desktop number (the 1280 section re-recorded byte-identical). (1) The first narrow sweep read 12,516 bleeds — 110 shell pages × 124 boxes of the docs shell's CLOSED off-canvas sidebar, parked at x:-288 behind an `overflow-x: hidden` shell, painting nothing. The bleed subject is now the box intersected with the padding box of every clipping ancestor: an empty slice is dropped, a slice that still crosses the edge is counted AT THE WIDTH IT PAINTS (a 400px child of a clipped card reports 45, not 325). (2) That left `recipes/sidebar` at 58 — its dismissed mobile drawer at translateX(-100%) with nothing clipping it. `inert` (not `aria-hidden`, which would also swallow every decorative icon) is the signal: a subtree that is not focusable, announced or clickable is not content the reader was offered. Both exemptions are pinned by a synthetic page where three panels sit at the SAME coordinates for three different reasons and only the stranded one — off-canvas with neither excuse, i.e. in the tab order and unreachable — is reported. (3) The sweep was flaky at 375 (1 run in 3): the sidebar controller reconciles to its closed drawer on init, starting a `transform` transition, and the collector was reading geometry mid-slide. Fixed by measuring the settled page — the sweep context now sets `reducedMotion: "reduce"` (the site's own recipes carry `transition: none` blocks for it, and it is what playwright.config.ts already throws for screenshots) and `settleMotion()` finishes every finite animation before collection, no sleeps in 372 page loads. Five consecutive green runs. The one hard wall stays desktop-only and says so ('no reference page has unreachable viewport bleed at desktop width'); 375 gets the ratchet, which is the point of the task — the numbers are recorded, not exempted, and 1.0R-07 spends them. Committed: 375×812 at 52 bleeds over 8 pages (dashboard-shell 14, settings-page 13, menubar 8, pagination 5, empty-state 4, input-otp 4, key-value 2, toast 2) and 3 overlaps; 1280×900 unchanged at 0/0/0/0/0 over 186 pages. That is a SUPERSET of the review's six — boxes, not one px number per page, and it reaches the inline start, where a right-edge measure cannot look. Verified: 8/8 playwright layout-lint (5 repeat runs), 65 bun cases in layout-lint+rhythm (13 new), typecheck. Three promises the frontmatter made and the body did not keep, all three closed by derivation rather than by writing the missing prose. (1) The CLI list was hand-written and five commands behind the registry — doctor, variant, scaffold, dev, bindings were dispatched by the CLI and invisible to the skill. Fixed at the source: src/command-registry.ts now holds COMMAND_DEFINITIONS, one entry per command carrying handler + category + args + summary + skillNote, so the TYPE makes it impossible to register a command without the metadata both readers need; COMMANDS is derived from it for dispatch, src/index.ts's HELP_CATEGORIES (the second, drifting copy) is deleted and `faqir help` groups straight off the registry, and renderCliReference() emits `faqir <name> <args>  # <skillNote>` per category. (2) `faqir scaffold` was never named in the body at all, so an agent asked for an invoice hand-composed one instead of running the print-tested generator. The catalogue moved out of src/commands/scaffold.ts into a side-effect-free src/scaffolds/registry.ts (SCAFFOLDS, SCAFFOLD_NAMES, DOCUMENT_SCAFFOLD_NAMES); both the command's --help and the new Scaffolds section read it, and the section states the FAQIR_REPLACE convention so the placeholders are usable. (3) Not one of the twelve shipped themes was named, so "make it dark" had nothing to pass. The Themes section is a row per registry/themes/*.theme.json with the manifest's own mood / scheme / dark_mode / pairs_with — the agent-selectable axis those manifests exist for. Both sections go into the project skill too, which is what keeps the CLI reference's pointers resolvable in both. The frontmatter gained the theme claim it was missing, and FRONTMATTER_CAPABILITIES pairs each advertised capability with the section that delivers it — asserted in both directions, since the frontmatter is the routing surface and a promise with nothing behind it routes work to a skill that cannot answer it. Tests: 21 new cases across four describes — every COMMAND_NAMES entry documented and nothing invented, each command's own args/gloss verbatim, a synthetic command/scaffold/theme.json each picked up with no generator edit, every theme row cross-read against its manifest, and every dark-moods theme confirmed to have a real .css to pass. Verified: 63 pass in skill.test.ts (mutation-checked — dropping one theme row fails four cases), 3436/3437 full suite, typecheck, check:skill, check:docs, smoke. The freeze, with a mechanism. SPEC-1.0.md is a NEW document rather than a section of FAQIR-SPEC.md — that file is 2,400 lines of design record, and a frozen contract cannot live inside a document that is free to keep changing; §2 there now opens with a pointer saying which of the two is normative. The spec says only what an implementation must do: the five attributes with their owner/vocabulary/enforcing-rule per row, one shared value grammar (^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$, never a list — which is what keeps [data-variant="x"] an equality match), the three sanctioned token modifiers (data-density compact|comfortable, data-motion enter|enter-active|leave|leave-active, data-theme light|dark|auto) as attributes that are frozen WITHOUT being a sixth protocol attribute, the v0.8 data-<attr>-<tier> suffix derived from the canon, manifest schema 1.0, enforcement, the amendment process, and the 0.x changelog. The half that makes it survive: src/protocol.ts carries the same contract as DATA (ATTRIBUTE_SPECS, TOKEN_MODIFIERS, PROTOCOL_RULES, RESPONSIVE_RULES, AMENDMENT_RULES, SCHEMA_CHANGELOG), the spec places an HTML-comment marker above each normative table, and tests/spec/protocol-1.0.test.ts (39 cases) parses them back out and compares row for row in both directions — prose that agrees with the engine only on the day it was written is exactly what a freeze cannot survive. Executable documentation is taken literally: EVERY fenced block is verified by the checker that fits it — seven html examples audit to zero findings at every severity against the shipped manifests, the css block is asserted to obey the attribute-selector rule it demonstrates, the json block validates against the schema's own variant/prop definitions, the text grammar block is compared to the compiled pattern, and an unrecognised fence language FAILS rather than being quietly exempted. The registry is checked in the other direction too: every data-part, data-state, data-variant and data-size value the 86 components ship is asserted to obey the published grammar. Schema: schema_version 1.0 (not 1.0.0 — the patch digit says nothing under 'additive only'; the file had claimed 1.0.0 since its first commit, before there was a freeze to back it, and the changelog row records that rather than tidying it away), plus stability, protocol_version, amendment_policy pointing at the #amendments anchor the page actually emits, and its own changelog array mirroring src/protocol.ts. Site: one versioned prefix built from PROTOCOL_VERSION rather than written out — spec/1.0/index.html (generated from the module, rendering the same example bytes the suite audited), spec/1.0/spec.md (byte-identical to the repo file) and spec/1.0/manifest.schema.json (byte-identical to the $id alias, which stays as the always-newest-1.x pointer). All three joined docs-agents.test.ts's hand-written literal path contract and the generated _headers. Two absorbed consequences: the skill header states the schema version so its test stopped asserting a three-part shape, and src/version.ts gained PROTOCOL_VERSION/SCHEMA_VERSION beside VERSION, which changed the committed browser audit bundle (rebuilt). Verified: 3,377 bun tests, typecheck, all seven check:* gates, audit:registry clean, 2,985 axe cases (up 8 — the new page in light+dark across the exemption-free sweep), layout-lint re-recorded at 186 pages with every ratcheted count still 0, docs-switcher green. PRE-EXISTING, NOT CAUSED HERE: a handful of visual-matrix baselines are stale locally (they are git-ignored and CI seeds them; pattern__auth-form__document__light__ltr reproduces on a clean tree), and `faqir <cmd> --json` subprocesses in tests/commands/json-output.test.ts intermittently spin at 100% CPU when spawned from the full-suite process — observed on a clean tree before any edit in this session, and green when the file runs alone.

The measurement, and the parity hole that hid it. `src/utils/layout-lint.ts` reduces "cramped" to four conditions over rectangles — gutter, seam, bleed, overlap — pure and `node:*`-free so 28 `bun test` cases drive it from literal boxes in both directions while `tests/visual/layout-lint.pw.ts` drives the same code over all 180 generated docs pages at 1280×900. Committed budget: 79 zero-gutter, 42 seam-bearing pages, 183 seams, 7 bleeds, 3 overlaps. It disagrees with the phase header's estimate in three places and each is argued rather than reconciled: a centred measure column IS a gutter (so `document`/`form-page`/`wizard` count, 79 not 84); only stacked BLOCK demos can seam (a row of badges is 0.9-08's problem, 183 not 187); and bleed asks reachability, not clipping — 122 long `<code>` lines behind a live scrollbar are not findings (counting them would put a floor under a number 0.9-11 must drive to zero), which also means `carousel`'s eight slides are a gutter finding rather than a bleed one, while seven boxes at x=−4 inside `sidebar`/`dashboard-shell` are genuinely unreachable and are. A ratchet, not a wall: `compareBudget` fails a rise naming the pages responsible, passes a fall as printed slack, and `lint:layout:update` refuses to record a rise, so the file can only ever describe a better site. Then the parity fix: the visual harness's `body { padding: 24px }` AND its `main.vr-root` flex column with `gap: 16px` are gone — the second was the same lie in a more damaging form, since a 16px gap between demos is exactly what a seam hunter must not add — leaving a document that injects no CSS at all, pinned by a new `matrix.test.ts` case. Everything re-baselined: `test:visual` green as a whole at 4 243 tests, which resolves 0.8-14; its "non-default theme cells" half turned out to be a partial LOCAL set (the baselines are git-ignored, CI seeds them per §12.2), documented in tests/visual/README.md.
